title: Welcoming a guest who arrives by taxi at Anne
grammarFocus: Polite greetings; May I have…?; We will reimburse up to…; numbers and yen
summary: Japan-site customers arrive by taxi at the Anne shop. Confirm the name/reservation, ask for the taxi receipt, and explain reimbursement up to ¥3,000.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. Welcome to ODAL Rent-a-Car at Anne. May I have your name and reservation, please?

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: Yes. Tanaka Yuki. I came by taxi from the airport.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Thank you. May I have your taxi receipt? For Japan-site customers, we reimburse the taxi fare up to 3,000 yen.

hints.ja: 支給・返金（タクシー代）

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: Here it is. The fare was about 2,300 yen.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Perfect. We will reimburse up to 3,000 yen with this receipt. Please complete check-in here at Anne first.

exercises.sentence: We will reimburse the taxi fare ___ to 3,000 yen.
exercises.explanation: up to + amount = maximum reimbursement.

exercises.prompt: Which arrival rule fits Japan-site customers?
choices: Free inbound airport shuttle from stop 14
Taxi to the Anne shop; up to ¥3,000 reimbursed with a receipt
Walk from headquarters at Akamine with no receipt
Always unpaid taxi with no reimbursement
exercises.explanation: Japan-site pages: taxi to Anne; up to ¥3,000 with receipt. Free stop-14 shuttle is for Korean-site (odal.co.kr) customers.
May I have… please? is a polite counter request.

options: Give money paper.
May I have your taxi receipt? We reimburse up to 3,000 yen.
exercises.explanation: Name the document and the exact yen limit.

title: Giving taxi-driver directions to Anne
grammarFocus: Imperatives and sequence words; prepositions; Please tell the driver…
summary: Help a lost guest find Anne: Nakachi intersection toward Itoman, past Teruya Motors, then left. Or search Google Maps for かりゆしレンタル Anne / ODALレンタカー那覇空港店.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: I am in a taxi near the airport. How do I find your shop?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Please tell the driver: from Nakachi intersection, go straight about one kilometer toward Itoman. After Teruya Motors, turn left immediately.

hints.ja: 運転手さんにこう伝えてください

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: You can also search Google Maps for “かりゆしレンタル Anne” or “ODALレンタカー 那覇空港店.” Do not go to headquarters — pickup is not possible there.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: So I check in at Anne first?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Yes. Reception is at Anne, 208-2 Zayasu, SOUTH ZA I 1F. The car lot is nearby but separate.

exercises.sentence: Please ___ the driver to turn left after Teruya Motors.
exercises.explanation: Please tell + person + to-infinitive for relaying directions.

choices: Enter only the phone 098-851-4326 in car navi — it always shows Anne
Search Google Maps for ODALレンタカー那覇空港店; phone navi may show headquarters instead
Pickup is at headquarters in Akamine
There is no Anne office
exercises.explanation: Japanese access page: phone in car navi can show HQ; pickup/return are not at headquarters.
Sequence words (then) keep multi-step directions clear.

options: Somewhere left maybe.
Please search Google Maps for かりゆしレンタル Anne, then come to reception first.
exercises.explanation: Give a searchable place name and the first step (reception).

title: Check-in and documents (two guest types)
grammarFocus: Could/would/please; I’m afraid we can’t…; must / have to
summary: Japanese/resident guests: original driver’s license. Korean/foreign guests: IDP and home-country license as required. No license in hand means no insurance coverage.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Could you show me your driver’s license, please? Every driver must bring the original.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: I am visiting from Korea. I have an English-language Korean license.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: For foreign visitors, please show your International Driving Permit and your home-country license. I’m afraid an English-language license alone is not enough.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: If you do not have the required license with you, insurance and coverage do not apply, and we cannot rent the car.

exercises.sentence: I’m afraid an English-language license alone is ___ enough.
exercises.explanation: I’m afraid + negative softens a document refusal.

exercises.prompt: What happens if the license is not in hand (Japan-site guide)?
choices: Coverage still applies
Insurance and coverage do not apply
Only a 500 yen fee
Staff can invent a temporary permit
exercises.explanation: Japanese booking guide: no license with them = insurance/coverage do not apply.
Could you… please? is standard polite counter English.

options: License now.
Could you show me your original driver’s license, please?
exercises.explanation: Polite request + original clarifies the rule.

title: The guest forgot the license or IDP
grammarFocus: Conditionals; softening bad news
summary: Without the required license/IDP, the car cannot be released. Do not mix cancellation tables — Japan-site vs Korean-site fees differ; confirm Japan-site percentages with a manager before quoting.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: I left my license at the hotel. Can I still rent today?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: I’m sorry. If you don’t have the required license with you, we cannot rent the car.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: What about the cancellation fee?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: It depends on your booking channel. For Korean-site bookings, same-day cancel is 50% of the amount paid, up to 100,000 KRW. For Japan-site bookings, please wait — I need to confirm the fee table with a manager before I quote a percentage.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: On both channels, a flight cancelled by natural disaster can be fully refunded with the proper documents.

exercises.sentence: If you don’t have the license, we ___ rent the car.
exercises.explanation: If + present, cannot + verb states a real consequence.

exercises.prompt: How should staff handle Japan-site cancel fees in class dialogues?
choices: Always quote 100% as proven fact with no caveat
Keep it general or say they must confirm with a manager before quoting
Use only the Korean 50% table for everyone
Say there is never a fee
exercises.explanation: JA research flags wording overlap with Anne clothing; confirm with a manager before quoting.
I’m sorry + clear result softens bad news.

options: Japan cancel is definitely 100% forever, trust me.
For Japan-site bookings, let me confirm the cancellation table with a manager before I quote the fee.
exercises.explanation: Uncertain policies must not be stated as hard facts.

title: Registering an additional driver
grammarFocus: can / may; anyone who will drive; present perfect
summary: Every driver must be registered. On the Japanese guide, adding a driver on site requires the original or a copy of the license.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: Can my husband drive too?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Yes. Anyone who will drive must be registered. You may add him now.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Have you both brought your licenses? For an on-site add, we need the original or a copy of his license.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: Yes — here is a copy.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Thank you. Unregistered drivers are not covered.

exercises.sentence: ___ you both brought your licenses?
exercises.explanation: Have you brought…? checks preparation before departure.

choices: Anyone who will drive must be registered.
Anyone who will driving must be registered.
Anyone who drive must registered.
Anyone will drive must to register.
exercises.explanation: Relative clause + must + be registered.
may = polite permission.

options: Maybe he drive, whatever.
Yes — we can register him if he shows his license now.
exercises.explanation: State permission and the document condition together.

title: Explaining insurance and NOC
grammarFocus: Conditionals; passives; included vs not covered
summary: Comprehensive insurance is included. NOC peace-of-mind plan is included (¥20,000 / ¥50,000 would-be fees). Quote exclusion fee ranges for the correct customer group.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: Is insurance included? What is NOC?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Yes. Comprehensive automobile insurance is included. All ODAL customers are enrolled in the NOC peace-of-mind plan, so there is no self-pay for that loss-of-use fee when the plan applies.

hints.ja: ノンオペレーションチャージ

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: If you have an accident and can drive back, that fee would normally be 20,000 yen. If a tow truck is needed, it would be 50,000 yen.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: What if I put the wrong fuel in?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Wrong fuel is not covered. For Japan-site contracts, the billed range on our Japanese graphic is about 50,000 to 90,000 yen at actual cost. Korean-site pages list a higher maximum — I will confirm which contract you have before I quote a number.

exercises.sentence: Comprehensive insurance ___ included in the rental fee.
exercises.explanation: is included = already part of the rental.

exercises.prompt: Japan-site wrong-fuel range on the official graphic?
choices: Always exactly ¥150,000
Free
Only 1,000 KRW
exercises.explanation: Japanese insurance graphic: wrong fuel ¥50,000–¥90,000. Do not mix with Korean-site maxima unless citing that group.
when the plan applies keeps the condition clear.

options: Every fee is the same for every website forever.
NOC of 20,000 or 50,000 yen is already covered when the plan applies; exclusion ranges can differ by booking channel.
exercises.explanation: Shared NOC amounts; label group-specific exclusion ranges.

title: Child seat for a child under 6
grammarFocus: must / have to / are required to; offers
summary: Japanese law requires a child seat under 6. Free at ODAL. Covers are cleaned before every rental. Offer installation help.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Will any child under six ride with you?

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: Yes. Do we have to use a seat?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Yes. Children under six are required to use a child seat. Child seats are free, and the covers are cleaned before every rental.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Would you like me to help install it in a rear seat?

exercises.sentence: Would you like me ___ help install it?
exercises.explanation: Would you like me to + verb = polite offer.

choices: Children under six must to use a child seat.
Children under six are required to use a child seat.
Children under six can required use a seat.
Children under six should required using a seat.
exercises.explanation: are required to + verb states legal obligation.
Simple present states a standing offer.

options: Install it yourself.
Would you like me to help install it?
exercises.explanation: Would you like…? sounds helpful.

Shall we walk around the car together before you leave?
exercises.explanation: Polite shared inspection builds trust.

title: How to start the car and free loan items
grammarFocus: Imperatives and sequencing; Make sure you…

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Inside you will find a phone charging stand, cables, a mini cooler with an ice pack, a sunshade, an eco bag, and a sand-play set.

Stroller rental guaranteed today
Cash envelope with 10,000 yen

Please return the cooler, sunshade, eco bag, and sand set with the car.

title: ETC and highway tolls (split by contract)

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: On Okinawa expressways, the maximum speed is 80 kilometers per hour.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: What about Korean-site ODAL bookings?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: For Korean-site ODAL customers, a free ETC card and unlimited Okinawa expressway tolls are included. Insert the card before you leave, and enter the ETC lane at 20 km/h or below.

exercises.sentence: If you don’t have an ETC card, enter a ___ lane.
exercises.explanation: general lane = non-ETC lane on the Japanese graphic.

choices: Japan-site and Korean-site ETC rules are identical
Japan-site: ETC usually not provided; Korean-site ODAL: free ETC and unlimited tolls
Nobody may use expressways
ETC is always cash only
exercises.explanation: Major operational split — do not mix customer groups.
Present simple for standing rules.

Let me check your booking channel — Japan-site and Korean-site ETC rules are different.

title: Driving advice (Maps, bus lanes, Kokusai-dori)
grammarFocus: should / I recommend; present simple for rules; time expressions
summary: Recommend Google Maps and left-side driving. Warn about Route 58 bus lanes and the Sunday 12:00–18:00 vehicle ban on Kokusai-dori.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: I recommend that you use Google Maps. In Japan, we drive on the left.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Please watch bus lanes on Route 58 on weekday mornings and evenings. Driving in the bus lane during those hours is a violation.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: On Kokusai-dori, general vehicles are banned every Sunday from 12:00 to 18:00. If your hotel is there, check parking access in advance.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: When should we pick up after landing?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: We recommend picking up one hour or more after your flight lands.

exercises.sentence: I recommend that you ___ Google Maps.
exercises.explanation: I recommend that you + base verb.

exercises.prompt: Which Kokusai-dori rule is on the Japanese graphic?
choices: Cars banned every Sunday 12:00–18:00 on the pedestrian zone section
Cars banned only at 03:00 Monday
No rules on Sundays
Only buses banned forever
exercises.explanation: RP06: Sunday 12:00–18:00 general-vehicle ban on the pedestrian zone.

You should avoid the Route 58 bus lane during weekday rush hours.
exercises.explanation: should + clear time window.

title: Changing or cancelling a booking
grammarFocus: Comparatives; percentages; as long as

dialogue.text: What if I cancel today?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: For Korean-site ODAL bookings, cancel up to one day before is a full refund; same-day is 50% of the amount paid, up to 100,000 KRW.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: For Japan-site bookings, our guide shows a different table. Before I quote a percentage, I need to confirm with a manager. On both channels, a flight cancelled by natural disaster can be fully refunded.

title: Typhoon or delayed flight
grammarFocus: First conditionals; in case / if; polite reassurance
summary: Cancelled flight can be refunded. Delayed arrivals may need flexible pickup. Mid-rental free extension details: Korean-site — label if used.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: Our flight may be cancelled because of a typhoon.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: You don’t need to worry. If the airline cancels the flight because of a natural disaster, the rental can be fully refunded.

dialogue.speaker: customer
dialogue.text: And if we are only delayed?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: If your arrival is delayed, please tell us the new time when you can. Shuttle overtime is often caused by late flights, so updates help us plan.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: Detailed mid-rental free extension rules for typhoons are on the Korean site — I will confirm whether they apply to your booking.
